name: Structure in conversation
description: Decides, by code from the move a turn calls for and the records the system holds, what structure a reply to a person carries: the problem it serves, what good looks like, the alternatives to compare, the one metric that shows which works and the next milestone, built on what is already held and proposing only what is missing, with at most one offer to keep it.
purpose: Give a person grounded clarity in a conversation by building the reply on the structure of their intent, and stay out of the way when a turn needs none.
approach: Take the move the turn calls for and the records held, show each part from the records first and from the caller's draft for what is missing, never state a metric value the records do not hold, and offer at most one batch of ensure-one additions for the missing pieces.
out_of_scope: Classifying the turn into a move (the planner does that), writing the reply (the Response Writer does that), applying an accepted offer (ESOI Application does that) and finding which solutions a request concerns (Relevant Solutions does that).
milestones: 1. Turns labelled with the move they call for get that move's structure from the records first, a plain turn gets none, no duplicate is added, a value is only ever one the records hold and at most one offer is made (metric-structure-in-conversation).
measures_of_success: A reply makes the structure move its turn calls for and no other, reuses what is held and offers at most one way to keep what is missing.
inputs: The move (none, frame, compare, review or focus), the records held as {table: {id: row}}, the relevant solution ids, the caller's draft of the missing pieces, the offers declined before and the solutions held as the person's own.
outputs: The move, the structure block (problem, ideal, solution, alternatives, metric with its value, milestone; each marked existing or proposed) and at most one offer: a key, the pieces it keeps and the ordered ensure-one edits.
effects: None: it only decides; an accepted offer is applied by ESOI Application.
usage_notes: Construct an arm and call `decide(turn)`. A reply is written from the block, and the same block is what a screen shows. Existing records are never edited: a held solution gets no milestone, and a declined offer key is not made again. The words a reply uses are in `terms.py`; the advisory judged checks of a reply are in `advisory.py` and are not part of the metric.
